title: Experience of using the fifth edition of the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC-V) on a sample of Russian children
abstract: Context and relevance. Timely and adequate diagnostics of children's cognitive abilities is an important and urgent task facing psychologists working in the field of education and health care, as well as providing psychological counseling. The version of the WISC, currently widely used for quantitative diagnostics of intelligence in Russia, is significantly outdated and is an adaptation of the first edition of the test, released in the middle of the last century. Cognitive tests created without taking into account the developmental characteristics of children may not include an assessment of abilities relevant to the current situation of development and significantly distort the diagnosis. Obviously, it is more appropriate to use more modern methods in assessing the intelligence of children of the alpha generation. Objective. This study describes and analyzes the experience of using the fifth edition of the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC-V) on a sample of modern Russian children. Hypothesis. This version of the Wechsler test for children is more consistent with modern requirements for assessing the intelligence in children. Methods and materials. The sample of the present study consisted of 182 children living in Moscow and the Moscow region, age M = 107.5 months; SD = 26.4 months (48% boys). All children were tested for intelligence using the WISC-V. Results. A data normality check, an analysis of mean values for subtests and indices, as well as correlation and factor analyses were conducted. The results indicated that the distribution of the Full Scale IQ did not deviate from normality. All subtest scores demonstrated significant correlations with the primary index scales. However, the mean values for both subtests and primary index scales were higher compared to the data from the American sample. Conclusions. The fifth edition of the Wechsler Intelligence Scale for Children (WISC-V) aligns more closely with contemporary psychodiagnostic standards, providing a comprehensive assessment of various cognitive characteristics, including fluid intelligence, working memory, and processing speed. However, for full adaptation of the test in Russia, an expansion of the sample and clarification of the norms is required.
